request.spec:
The screen gains a header with counters, shown at all times: the number of people on the sheet
(retired people included), the number of claims in each status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED,
VOID), the sheet's due-total and the sheet's overdue-total. Each counter always equals the figure
it repeats: the status counts those of the summary, the two totals the sheet's totals.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The screen gains a header with counters, shown at all times: the number of people on the sheet
(retired people included), the number of claims in each status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED,
VOID), the sheet's due-total and the sheet's overdue-total. Each counter always equals the figure
it repeats: the status counts those of the summary, the two totals the sheet's totals.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The screen now has a header with the counters, and all 4 tests in the acceptance spec pass under `bin/e2e`.

The header sits at the top of a loaded sheet and shows the number of people (retired people included), the number of claims in each status from DRAFT to VOID, the sheet's due-total and its overdue-total. It carries the `header-*` test ids the spec expects.

**Why the counters can't drift:** I moved the sheet's figures out of `PeopleList.tsx` into one shared hook, `features/people/useSheetFigures.ts`. The people list, its totals, the summary panel and the new header (`features/header/SheetHeader.tsx`) all read from it now. So each header counter is computed by exactly the same code as the figure it repeats.

**What I changed:**
- `PeopleList.tsx` and `SummaryPanel.tsx` now use the shared hook. The summary takes a status-count function instead of the raw claims list.
- `routes/index.tsx` puts the header first on a loaded sheet.

**What I didn't change:** the server, the stored data and the audit file. The header only repeats figures the app already loads, so it needed no new endpoint and writes no audit records.

When no sheet is loaded, the header isn't shown, because there are no figures to count.
